title: ARWP Search and Agent Recommendations Registry
scope: Source-backed recommendations for public websites that want to remain discoverable, citable and operable across classic search, generative search and browser agents.

methodology.principle: ARWP records upstream requirements, opportunities and measurable signals. Passing a rule never guarantees crawling, indexing, ranking, citation or agent success.

rules.title: Meet Google Search technical eligibility
rules.claim: Google documents three minimum technical requirements for indexing eligibility: Googlebot is not blocked, the page returns HTTP 200, and the page has indexable content. Eligibility does not guarantee indexing.
rules.automatedCheck: homepage HTTP success, robots access heuristic, noindex/X-Robots-Tag heuristic

rules.title: Preserve Search and snippet eligibility for Google generative features
rules.claim: Google states that supporting links in AI Overviews and AI Mode use the normal Search foundation: a page must be indexed and eligible to appear with a snippet, with no additional technical requirement specific to these AI features.

rules.title: Publish useful original, non-commodity content
rules.claim: Google's generative-search guidance emphasizes unique, useful and non-commodity content rather than special AI-only markup or an AEO/GEO shortcut.

rules.title: Offer a Google Preferred Sources control when relevant
rules.claim: Google provides an interactive button and a content-link flow that lets users add a domain or subdomain as a Preferred Source. Preferred-source indicators can appear in AI Mode and AI Overviews where the feature is available.
rules.automatedCheck: detect Google preferred-source script, declarative button attribute or preferences/source link
rules.notes: This is a user preference mechanism, not a general ranking guarantee.

rules.title: Keep section deep links addressable
rules.claim: Google recommends that content targeted by Read more deep links be immediately visible, that page-load JavaScript not force scroll position, and that History API or location.hash code not remove the fragment.
rules.automatedCheck: heading IDs plus suspicious fragment/scroll-reset patterns

rules.title: Publish accurate sitemap freshness metadata
rules.claim: Google supports sitemap lastmod when it is consistently and verifiably accurate and represents the last significant change to the page.
rules.automatedCheck: sitemap presence and syntactic lastmod observation; semantic accuracy remains manual

rules.title: Do not accidentally block OAI-SearchBot when ChatGPT Search visibility is desired
rules.claim: OpenAI says sites that want content included in ChatGPT Search summaries and snippets should allow OAI-SearchBot. Search crawling and GPTBot training controls are separate decisions.
rules.automatedCheck: robots.txt OAI-SearchBot and wildcard access heuristic

rules.title: Notify participating engines about changed URLs with IndexNow
rules.claim: IndexNow defines a mechanism for notifying participating search engines when a URL is added, updated or deleted.
rules.notes: ARWP must not imply that all search engines participate or that notification guarantees indexing.

rules.title: Measure Google generative-search visibility separately
rules.claim: Google Search Console exposes dedicated generative AI performance reporting for visibility in AI Overviews, AI Mode and related generative Search experiences.

rules.title: Measure AI citations and grounding queries in Bing Webmaster Tools
rules.claim: Bing Webmaster Tools AI Performance reports expose total citations, cited pages, grounding-query samples, page-level citation activity and trends across supported Microsoft AI experiences.

rules.title: Expose structured browser-agent tools only where they are useful and real
rules.claim: WebMCP lets web applications expose structured tools to browser agents instead of requiring agents to infer every action from visual UI. Chrome documents WebMCP as an origin-trial feature rather than a stable universal web requirement.
rules.automatedCheck: not assessed by static audit; requires explicit browser runtime

rules.title: Evaluate WebMCP tool selection, execution and security
rules.claim: Chrome's WebMCP guidance recommends evals before production and separate security review because browser-agent tools can be affected by prompt injection and other agent-specific risks.
rules.automatedCheck: not assessed by static audit; attach runtime eval receipts when available

rules.title: Track IETF AIPREF Content-Usage preferences without treating the draft as final
rules.claim: draft-ietf-aipref-attach-05 defines work-in-progress attachment mechanisms for AI usage preferences through a Content-Usage HTTP header field and a Content-Usage robots.txt rule.
rules.automatedCheck: observe Content-Usage in homepage response headers and robots.txt; absence is not a failure
rules.notes: Internet-Drafts can change or expire and must not be represented as an RFC.

rules.title: Track the W3C Introduction Layer Community Group as an upstream discovery candidate
rules.claim: The W3C-hosted Introduction Layer Community Group was launched in August 2026 to explore machine-native resource identity, purpose, constraints and responsible-party discovery for agents. Community Group work is not automatically a W3C Recommendation.

rules.title: Keep the publisher service map valid when ARWP is adopted
rules.claim: If a publisher chooses to expose an ARWP profile, it should validate and remain consistent with actually observable interfaces. ARWP profile presence itself is not a search ranking signal.
